title: Easy Parking: choose the visual world
question: The re-roll landed on the mall directory board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mall Directory Board
options.lineage: The backlit floor directory beside Bangkok mall escalators
options.thesis: Every lot reads like the directory you already trust: a stack of floor bands with a red dot marking where you are.
options.viewport: Dark slate top bar; left column is the floor stack (B2, B1, 1), each band showing free count and fill; right is the selected floor's map with the red dot on your slot.
options.risk: Floor colours compete with availability states if fill and the words ว่าง/เต็ม don't carry the status.

raised.raise: On a phone the current lot's free count owns the first screen; everything else is one scroll down.
Every floor map is drawn at the same scale, so floors compare at a glance.
Flat unmodulated colour only: no gradients, glass or drop shadows anywhere.
The red dot is reserved for the driver's own car or booked slot; nothing else is that red.
The floor badge is one object repeated at every size: nav, card, map and kiosk.

options.label: Car-Park Floor Paint
options.lineage: Painted bay lines, stencilled numbers and pillar level colours
options.thesis: The interface is painted like the deck itself: line-yellow on asphalt, stencilled bay numbers, a pillar colour for each level.
options.viewport: Charcoal shell, a big stencilled floor number with the free count beside it, the bay map as painted lines below.
options.risk: Yellow-on-asphalt is where most parking UIs land, so it's familiar more than distinct.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Availability as a departure board: one ruled row per floor, counts flipping character by character.
options.viewport: Black board top half: rows for B2/B1/1 with free count, rate and status; light work area below for plate search and the map.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: car parks already post LED counts at the gate, so clarity holds. It loses on audience fit because it reads as a train station.
options.risk: Becomes a costume if the flaps go past the counts into the controls.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One lot owns the screen; swipe for the next.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no imagery to fill the frame, and admins can't work in a feed.
options.kept: The current lot's free count owns the phone's first screen.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject at fixed scale through its stages.
options.case: Fuses poorly: drivers don't identify with it and it reads as editorial.
options.kept: Every floor map at the same scale.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.case: Fuses poorly: parking floors are rectangles, and lobes blur the bays.
options.kept: Flat unmodulated colour; no gradients or shadows.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain in standard inks, the course in purple.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a niche sport's notation that drivers would have to learn.
options.kept: One colour reserved for the driver's own route and slot.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Coarse pixel letterforms at poster scale.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the Thai script has no good bitmap display faces, and it reads as retro.
options.kept: The floor badge is one object repeated at every size.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean parking app, as the category ships it, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: White top bar, search, three floor cards with green/amber/red bars, map below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every parking app by design.
